inputs.note: Model now uses MID-CYCLE FCF of $50m (not FY2025 peak $79m) as the base year FCF. This is supported by 8-year FCF history showing range $2.7m (FY2023) to $79m (FY2025), mean $32m, median $23m, mean ex-cyclone $37m. The $50m mid-cycle estimate sits between long-run historical average and recent peak, recognising structural improvements from automation and lower debt while not assuming FY2025 record is the new normal.

trip_reasons: Base case upside 354% with current price ($5.01) in upper half of 10yr range ($2.31-$6.18)
sanity_check.diagnosis: Peak-FCF extrapolation (FY2025 OCF $79m is 2.4x historical median $32m) combined with WACC understatement (11% did not capture Zespri single-desk concentration, NZX small-cap illiquidity, or weather cyclicality - structural risks the market has priced for 10+ years)
sanity_check.fix_applied: Switched to mid-cycle FCF $50m (between historical median $32m and recent peak $79m). Raised WACC from 11% to 14% by adding structural premiums: Zespri concentration +2%, NZX illiquidity +2%, weather cyclicality +1.5%. Added exit-multiple caps per scenario (5x bear, 6x base, 7x bull).

valuation_philosophy.approach: Mid-cycle FCF DCF with elevated WACC reflecting structural risks, plus exit-multiple sanity cap on terminal value
valuation_philosophy.why_not_peak_fcf: Previous model used FY2025 peak FCF ($79m) and produced IV of $22.75 - implying 30x P/E and 3.4x P/B. Seeka's historical price multiples (10 years) have NEVER exceeded 0.99x P/B or 7.8x EV/EBITDA. The market consistently discounts Seeka because: (1) Zespri concentration - ~60% of revenue flows through a single-desk export monopoly with no alternative customer; (2) NZX small-cap illiquidity - $220m market cap, thin trading, 44m shares; (3) extreme weather cyclicality - EBITDA range $26m-$96m in 3 years. These are STRUCTURAL discounts that will not unwind.
structural_discounts_applied: Zespri single-desk concentration premium: +2.0% to WACC (60% of revenue through a regulated monopoly customer; no pricing power, no alternative outlets, regulatory dependency)
NZX small-cap illiquidity premium: +2.0% to WACC ($220m market cap, ~44m shares, thin trading)
Weather/cyclicality premium: +1.5% to WACC (EBITDA ranged 3.7x in 3 years; no earnings floor)
valuation_philosophy.calibration: Base IV $7.93 implies 10.4x P/E and 1.17x P/B - just above the historical P/B ceiling of 0.99x. This is defensible given the structural balance sheet improvements (net debt down 42% from peak) and capacity for higher mid-cycle earnings post-automation. The market is currently pricing Seeka near the upper bound of its 10-year price range ($2.31-$6.18), having already rerated upward on FY2025 results.

historical_multiples.note: Historical FY-end share price applied to that year's actuals. Demonstrates the structural discount the market applies. FY2023 cyclone year excluded from averages.

current_at_501.interpretation: P/B and EV/EBITDA are NEAR HISTORICAL AVERAGES, not depressed. The market has already rerated Seeka upward on FY2025 results (price up from $3.27 at Dec 2024 to $5.01 today, +53%). The 'cheap' P/E of 6.6x reflects investor expectation that FY2025 peak earnings will normalise, not that the market has missed something.

fcf_history.interpretation: FCF range is extreme: $2.7m (cyclone) to $79m (record). The 8-year mean of $32m and ex-cyclone mean of $37m are below FY2024-2025 levels because automation and capacity expansion structurally lifted the earnings floor. A mid-cycle estimate of $50m respects both the long-run history and the structural improvements, while being deliberately conservative versus FY2025 peak.

historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Through-cycle growth set at 3-5% reflecting NZ kiwifruit industry volume trajectory (Zespri 5-year plan: +10% by 2030 = ~2% pa volume) plus modest yield/automation tailwind. Equity and revenue CAGRs (11%+) are inflated by cyclical recovery and not sustainable. EPS 5yr CAGR (7.9%) is the more sober metric and itself reflects favourable endpoints (FY2025 record). Through-cycle growth must be modest because: (1) capacity is largely built; (2) industry growth is single-digit; (3) margin expansion is mature.

base.fcf_base_year_rationale: Mid-cycle FCF of $50m. Below FY2025 record ($79m) but above 8-year mean ($32m). Recognises automation and lower debt have lifted the floor while respecting cyclicality.
base.growth_rationale: Through-cycle volume growth aligned with Zespri's 10% industry growth target to 2030 (~2% pa) plus 1-2pp from automation efficiency gains and Australian/Raukokore orchard ramp. Deliberately modest - reflects mature operations.
base.wacc_rationale: NZ 10yr risk-free 4.2% + beta ERP (1.1x 7%) = 11.9% + Zespri concentration premium 2.0% + NZX small-cap illiquidity premium 2.0% + weather cyclicality premium 1.5% - leverage benefit 3.6% (improved BS) = ~14.0%. This is higher than typical NZ small-cap DCFs because the structural discounts are real and persistent: the market has applied them for 10+ years.
base.terminal_growth_rationale: Below NZ long-run GDP growth (~2.5%). Reflects mature NZ kiwifruit industry, climate change headwinds in BoP growing region, and gradual Northern Hemisphere SunGold competition emerging.
base.exit_multiple_cap_rationale: Cap terminal value at 6x EV/EBITDA (above 10yr historical average of 5.6x but well below the all-time max of 7.8x). Acts as sanity check against Gordon Growth assumptions producing unrealistic terminal multiples.

bull.fcf_base_year_rationale: Recognises FY2024-25 structural improvements may have permanently lifted Seeka's earnings power. $65m is below FY2025 peak but above the FY2024-25 average, reflecting confidence in automation/scale benefits.
bull.growth_rationale: Bull case: industry tracks toward upper Zespri targets, Reemoon automation delivers ahead of expectations, Australian orchards contribute materially, market begins to value the structurally improved business.
bull.wacc_rationale: Modest WACC reduction as balance sheet continues to improve, dividend track record establishes, automation de-risks operations. Still above typical industrials WACC due to persistent Zespri concentration and NZX illiquidity discounts.
bull.terminal_growth_rationale: Slightly above base case reflecting market share gains from smaller competitors and successful Australian expansion.
bull.exit_multiple_cap_rationale: Bull case allows terminal to reach the historical maximum multiple (7.8x in 2017) - a high but not unprecedented re-rating.

bear.fcf_base_year_rationale: Bear case base year reflects a cyclical downturn. Below long-run mean but above FY2023 cyclone trough. Represents a poor-but-not-extreme operating environment.
bear.growth_rationale: Bear case: FY2026 is a poor growing season (-15% from base year $35m = $30m), gradual recovery, but structural headwinds (Northern Hemisphere SunGold, climate change in BoP) limit upside to 3-5%.
bear.wacc_rationale: Higher WACC reflects covenant stress risk, potential dividend suspension, and re-rating risk if market questions earnings sustainability. Bear case effectively asks: what discount rate would investors require if the FY2023 scenario repeats?
bear.terminal_growth_rationale: Subdued terminal growth as climate change accelerates, Northern Hemisphere supply competition intensifies, and grower defections to co-op competitors continue.
bear.exit_multiple_cap_rationale: Bear case caps at 5x EV/EBITDA - below the 10-year average. Reflects a market that has lost confidence in the cyclical recovery story.

base.interpretation: Base case terminal equity value per share of $9.13 implies an entry price of $4.54 to achieve 15% CAGR. Current $5.01 is 10% ABOVE this entry price - so 15% returns are not achievable at today's price under base case assumptions. To achieve 15% CAGR, wait for a pullback toward $4.50.

bull.interpretation: Bull case TV per share $17.86 supports an entry up to $8.88 for 15% CAGR. Current $5.01 is 44% below this - meaningful upside if the bull case plays out.

bear.interpretation: Bear case TV per share is only $3.20 - implying that under a poor scenario, no positive return is achievable at any price above $1.59. Current $5.01 is materially above this floor.

sensitivity.note: Intrinsic value per share (NZD) across WACC and terminal growth combinations. Uses base case mid-cycle FCF projections ($50m base year, 3-4% growth). Rows = WACC, Columns = terminal growth.

probability_weighted.rationale: Equal 25% weight for bull and bear reflects high earnings cyclicality. Base case at 50% reflects the most likely path of through-cycle operations. Weighted IV of $8.45 implies 69% upside - meaningful but realistic, in contrast to the prior peak-FCF model which produced 330% upside (and implied historically unprecedented multiples).

key_metrics_summary.note: Current multiples (P/E 6.6x, P/B 0.74x, EV/EBITDA 3.35x) are NEAR HISTORICAL AVERAGES, not depressed. P/B avg over 10yrs is 0.72x. EV/EBITDA avg is 5.6x - so on FY2025 peak EBITDA the stock looks 'cheap' but on mid-cycle EBITDA ($70m) the multiple is 4.6x, much closer to historical average. The 35.8% peak FCF yield drops to 22.7% on mid-cycle FCF - still attractive but reflects cyclical risk.

key_assumptions.fcf_definition: Operating Cash Flow used as Free Cash Flow proxy. FY2025 OCF was $79.0m but model uses $50m mid-cycle base to avoid extrapolating peak earnings.
key_assumptions.mid_cycle_rationale: 8-year OCF range $2.7m-$79m, mean $32m, ex-cyclone mean $37m. $50m represents the FY2024-2025 average ($72m) adjusted downward by 30% to recognise that record results are not the new normal. Above long-run mean to recognise structural improvements (automation reducing per-tray costs, capacity expansion, lower debt-service drag).
key_assumptions.wacc_components: Base 14.0%: NZ 10yr risk-free 4.2% + beta ERP 7.7% + Zespri concentration premium 2.0% + NZX small-cap illiquidity premium 2.0% + weather/cyclicality premium 1.5% - leverage benefit 3.4% = 14.0%. The structural premiums total 5.5% and explain why Seeka has never traded above 0.99x P/B in 10 years - the market is pricing these risks every day, not missing them.
key_assumptions.structural_discount_persistence: Zespri concentration is regulated under NZ Kiwifruit Export Regulations - unlikely to change. NZX small-cap illiquidity is structural for a $220m mcap. Weather cyclicality is the fundamental nature of the business. These will NOT unwind with time or strong results - they are permanent features.
key_assumptions.net_debt: Net bank debt of $100.3m at 31 December 2025 (bank borrowings $119.6m less cash $19.4m).
key_assumptions.exit_multiple_caps: Terminal value capped at scenario-specific EV/EBITDA multiples (5x bear, 6x base, 7x bull). These caps are based on 10-year historical range (3.2-7.8x, average 5.6x). In current model the Gordon Growth values are already below the caps, but the caps remain as a sanity check.
key_assumptions.valuation_date: 25 May 2026. Stock price NZ$5.01 fetched from Yahoo Finance.

strengths: Uses mid-cycle FCF ($50m) instead of FY2025 peak ($79m) - avoids extrapolating record earnings
WACC of 14% reflects Zespri concentration (+2%), NZX small-cap illiquidity (+2%), and weather cyclicality (+1.5%) - structural discounts the market has applied for 10+ years
Base IV of $7.93 implies 10.4x P/E and 1.17x P/B - within shouting distance of historical averages (P/E 13.1x, P/B 0.72x ceiling 0.99x)
Exit multiple cap (6x EV/EBITDA) prevents terminal value from implying unprecedented re-rating
Bear case IV ($2.70) is below current price - acknowledges genuine downside risk that prior model ignored
Probability-weighted IV of $8.45 implies 69% upside - meaningful but defensible
limitations: Mid-cycle FCF estimate is judgemental - $40-60m range is defensible
Structural discounts are large and may overstate persistent risk if Seeka successfully grows past small-cap status (unlikely in 5-year horizon)
Does not separately model dividend yield (current 10% trailing) as a return component
Bear case assumes orderly cyclical decline, not a tail event (covenant breach, equity raise, etc.)
Through-cycle growth assumption (3-4%) is conservative given Zespri's 10% industry growth target to 2030
dcf_quality_assessment.confidence_level: Moderate. The model now produces results aligned with 10+ years of market behaviour. Base case IV $7.93 implies the stock is moderately undervalued (58% upside), but not dramatically so. Entry price for 15% CAGR is $4.54 - 10% below current price - meaning today's price is fair-to-slightly-rich for a 15% target return. The investment case is now: collect ~10% dividend yield + modest capital appreciation + optionality on automation/Australian growth, NOT a 4-5x bagger.

investment_context.valuation_at_current_price: At $5.01, Seeka trades at 6.6x FY2025 peak earnings, 0.74x book, and a 10% trailing dividend yield. On mid-cycle earnings ($50m FCF, mid-cycle EBITDA ~$70m), the multiples are 4.6x EV/EBITDA and ~7% mid-cycle FCF yield - reasonable for a NZX small-cap with structural risks. The probability-weighted IV of $8.45 implies 69% upside.
investment_context.return_decomposition: Expected return at current $5.01: ~10% trailing dividend yield + 5-15% capital appreciation over 5 years = 12-15% total return CAGR in base case. This is consistent with the entry price analysis ($4.54 entry for 15% CAGR).
investment_context.key_question: Is the FY2024-2025 record-earnings cycle a NEW NORMAL (warranting peak-FCF DCF) or a CYCLICAL PEAK (warranting mid-cycle)? Three arguments for new normal: (1) automation structurally cut per-tray costs; (2) industry volumes are growing through 2030 per Zespri targets; (3) Seeka has captured operating leverage from capacity expansion. Three arguments for cyclical peak: (1) weather drove FY2024-25 record volumes; (2) FY2023 cyclone shows downside is large; (3) market is already pricing in the better outlook (price up 53% in 2025). This model takes the middle path.
catalyst_risks: FY2026 growing season outcome (earliest signal: August 2026 H1 results)
Reemoon automation installation performance during 2026 harvest
Australian orchard production ramp from new orchards entering production
NZ kiwifruit industry total tray count for 2026 season
Interest rate trajectory affecting WACC and debt service costs

methodology_notes.fcf_calculation: Through-cycle FCF starting from $50m mid-cycle, growing at 3-4% (volume + modest yield)
methodology_notes.cyclicality_adjustment: Base case uses mid-cycle starting point. Bull case starts from $65m (recognising structural improvements). Bear case starts from $35m (poor cyclical environment). FY2023 extreme case ($2.7m OCF) is NOT used as bear case - too tail-event-like.
methodology_notes.growth_rate_philosophy: Through-cycle growth set at 3-5% reflecting industry volume growth (Zespri targets ~2% pa industry volume) plus modest yield/automation tailwind. Historical CAGRs (10-11%) are inflated by cyclical recovery and not sustainable.
methodology_notes.wacc_philosophy: WACC raised from previous 11% to 14% to incorporate the structural discounts the market has consistently applied. The +5.5% in structural premiums (Zespri concentration, NZX illiquidity, weather cyclicality) reflect 10+ years of observed market behaviour.
methodology_notes.exit_multiple_sanity_check: Each scenario caps terminal value at a historical-range EV/EBITDA multiple (5x, 6x, 7x). In the current model the Gordon Growth values are below the caps, so caps are not binding.
methodology_notes.valuation_date: 25 May 2026. Stock price NZ$5.01 fetched from Yahoo Finance.
